A card that cannot proceed gets its question field filled with the structured decision-needed text (DECISION NEEDED, CONTEXT, OPTIONS, RECOMMENDATION, IMPACT IF UNANSWERED), blocked_on set to the person who owes the answer, status set to blocked, and the executor moves to the next eligible card in the same session. A recommendation is mandatory: a question without one is unfinished. HALT ON AN ABSENT TOOL OR A FALSE PREMISE, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT RULE AND IS NOT SOFTENED BY THE ONE ABOVE. Skip-not-halt covers a decision the executor lacks the authority to make. It does not cover a card whose premise is wrong. When a card names a tool, table, column, route, file, script, environment variable or service that does not exist, or asserts a fact the repository contradicts, the executor STOPS WORKING THAT CARD IMMEDIATELY. It does not build the missing thing on a guess, does not invent the tool, and does not reinterpret the card until it fits what is there. It sets status blocked, sets blocked_on to the person who owes the correction, and writes into question the structured decision-needed text naming the premise and PASTING THE COMMAND OUTPUT THAT DISPROVES IT, then moves to the next eligible card. status halted stays reserved for the failure ceiling in CLAUDE.md section 10 and is not used for this. When defaults covers an ambiguity the executor APPLIES IT AND LOGS THE APPLICATION IN NOTES, and does not ask. Defaults fill silence; they never override an explicit instruction in the card. ACCEPTANCE: every card names a machine-checkable acceptance line, a command with an expected exit code, a URL with expected content, or a named test. No acceptance, no ship. A card whose acceptance cannot be run yet is blocked, never shipped. A check that has never been seen to fail is not a check. MIGRATIONS: authored as supabase/migrations/NNNN_name.sql and listed in the PR description by path. WHO APPLIES ONE IS READ OFF CLAUDE.md SECTION 8 WHEN THE CARD IS PICKED AND IS NOT ASSERTED HERE, because that section changed three times in the four days before this board was written and this board is not worked for weeks. A migration file is never edited after it has been applied; a correction is a new numbered file. A BACKFILL AND A COLUMN DROP NEVER TRAVEL IN THE SAME MIGRATION, which is why P3-04b and P3-05b exist as separate cards. DENSITY DOCTRINE BINDS EVERY SCREEN CARD ON THIS BOARD, not only wave 4: summary first, detail behind a drill-in, never a full-length table dumped into a page. Ids sort lexically, which is why P3-04b sorts between P3-04 and P3-05. CONFLICTS ARE RESOLVED LOCALLY, AGAINST THE FULL TREE, WITH THE CHECKS RUN BEFORE THE COMMIT, per R-052 and CLAUDE.md section 3. cards.defaults: THE LIST IS ONE RPC AND NOT A POSTGREST QUERY, AND THAT IS FORCED BY THE FOLD. P3-06 asks for one search box, diacritic-folded, filtered SERVER SIDE. THE TOTAL COMES BACK WITH EVERY PAGE, as a window function over the filtered set. A separate count query is a second round trip that can disagree with the first under concurrent writes, and the footer would then claim a number of pages the list cannot produce. THE OPEN-PROJECT COUNT IS IN THE SAME PASS, which is the fifth of the five columns. Counting it per row afterwards is a query per page at best and a query per row at worst. OPEN MEANS NOT CLOSED AND NOT DEACTIVATED, AND SUSPENDED COUNTS. A stopped site is still a relationship in progress; leaving it out would make the column say a client has no work with the firm. AN UNKNOWN FILTER VALUE FALLS BACK TO THE DEFAULT AND DOES NOT ERROR. Somebody sends a stale link with ?stare=nonsense or ?pagina=abc and gets a list, not an error page. Both the SQL and parseClientQuery do this, deliberately, at both ends. cards.title: responder.sh stops consuming the owner's rulings: one process reads the bot, and rulings go through the same spool ASK-01 uses.
cards.plain: Fix the bot so that an answer sent while the assistant is replying to chat is not swallowed. At the moment a ruling can vanish before the part of the system that needs it ever sees it.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh` exits 0, extended with a case that PROVES the defect and its fix: a ruling-form message present in the same getUpdates batch as an ordinary chat message is still readable by inbox.mjs AFTER responder.sh has run. PLUS: no second process reads the bot; the PR names which single process calls getUpdates and shows that the other reads the spool.
cards.defaults: THE DEFECT IS LIVE AND IS IN THE OWNER'S OWN RULING PATH. scripts/poc/responder.sh polls getUpdates, classifies, deliberately does NOT answer ruling forms because inbox.mjs owns them, and then acknowledges the offset past EVERY update it read, including those rulings. Telegram deletes an update once getUpdates is called with an offset past it, so the ruling is gone before inbox.mjs ever runs. inbox.mjs already prints a line about exactly this failure mode, which is how long it has been known without being fixed. THE FIX SHAPE IS GIVEN BY THE OWNER: route rulings through the same spool ASK-01 uses, so ONE process reads the bot and the other reads a file. Which process keeps the socket is the card's to decide and to record. DO NOT FIX IT BY NARROWING THE OFFSET. Acknowledging only the messages the responder answered would leave ignored messages to be reclassified forever, which is the exact reason the current code acknowledges everything, and that comment is in the file. The answer is one reader, not a cleverer offset. PRIORITY ABOVE WAVE 3, on the owner's instruction: a broken ruling path means every later escalation can be silently lost.

THE FAILURE MODE THAT THE FIX ITSELF COULD HAVE INTRODUCED, AND THE GUARD FOR IT. cards.title: check:removal-safety, the guard for the direction INC-05's guard cannot see: deployed code still reading schema a pending migration removes.
cards.plain: Stop the system from deleting something out of the database while the live site is still asking for it. That mistake took the site down once already, and the existing safety check only looks the other way round.
cards.question:
DECISION NEEDED: can the applier assert that a fix is DEPLOYED, not merely merged, before a removal migration runs?
CONTEXT: the ordering rule is that a removal applies after the code that stops reading it is merged AND DEPLOYED. The merged half is asserted by check:removal-safety. The deployed half cannot be asserted from here: VERCEL_TOKEN exists in the permitted secret read but is EMPTY, and production exposes no endpoint reporting the commit it is serving. Inventing a substitute for 'deployed' is the exact class of guess that produced INC-06.
OPTIONS: (a) add a small public endpoint that reports the commit the live site is running, and have the applier read it; (b) provide a real VERCEL_TOKEN so the applier can ask the deployments API; (c) leave it as an operator statement, RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED=yes, recorded in the journal.
RECOMMENDATION: (a). It needs no new credential, it is the deployed build reporting its own identity rather than a proxy for it, and it works for any host.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: the applier refuses every removal migration on production unless the operator states the deploy has landed, which is safe and is the current behaviour. Nothing is blocked except unattended removals.
cards.acceptance: NAMED COMMAND: `npm run check:removal-safety` exits 0 on a clean tree and is wired into quality.yml as its own step. IT MUST BE PROVEN AGAINST BOTH INCIDENTS RECONSTRUCTED AS FIXTURES, and each must FAIL the check: the INC-05 forward case, merged code reading schema a pending migration ADDS, and the INC-06 reverse case, deployed code reading schema a pending migration REMOVES. The PR shows both failures and the clean pass. PLUS: the applier refuses to apply a batch containing a removal while the check is red, proven by a case in prove-applier.mjs. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults: INC-05 AND INC-06 ARE ONE DEFECT IN TWO DIRECTIONS AND EACH HAS COST AN OUTAGE. check:pending-schema-reads compares MERGED CODE against the PENDING REGISTER, so it guards additive drift only, by construction: it cannot see deployed code reading schema that was just removed, because that code is already on main and the register is already clear. ENUMERATE AGAINST THE TABLE, NEVER GREP THE COLUMN NAME WITH EXCLUSIONS. That filter is exactly what hid lib/data/extraction-actions.ts:269 during P3-05b, where a write to the products table lived in a file named for extraction and a grep excluding 'extraction' skipped it. Find every read and write of the TABLE first, then look inside those for the object. THE ORDERING RULE IS ENCODED AS A MACHINE CONDITION, NOT PROSE: additive migrations apply BEFORE the code that reads them merges; removal migrations apply AFTER the code that stops reading them is merged AND DEPLOYED. DEPLOYED IS NOT MERGED AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE OF INC-06. Whether the applier can assert deployment is a question for the owner and not for a proxy: there is no usable Vercel credential in the permitted secret read, and inventing a substitute for 'deployed' is the exact class of mistake this card exists to stop. Ask, do not guess.

cards.title: Deviz: create a version against a project and edit its lines from the product catalogue, with the quoted price frozen and the current price shown beside it.
cards.plain: Someone can build an estimate for a job by picking products off the real catalogue, and later see at a glance where the prices they quoted have drifted away from what those products cost today.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/deviz.spec.ts` exits 0. deviz.spec covers: a deviz is created against a project as version 1 in status Ciorna and persists with its lines; a second deviz on the same project is created as version 2 and the first is still readable; a line is added from the product catalogue with a quantity, and its unit price is WRITTEN from the catalogue at that moment; the price on a saved line does NOT change when the product catalogue price is then changed, and the row shows the quoted price, the current catalogue price and the difference between them as three separate values; THE NAMED CASE, WHICH IS THE ONE THE ADDENDUM ASKED FOR BY NAME: a deviz quoted in March still shows March prices in June; the same product cannot be added twice to one deviz; a line total, the subtotal, the Adaos row from margin_percent and the Total match the hand-calculated values; the unit shown on a line comes from the product and cannot be typed; a deviz in Ciorna is editable and a deviz in Emis, Acceptat, Respins or Expirat is not, with the refusal coming from the database and not only from a disabled button; a deviz whose valid_until has passed while still Emis is shown with a Romanian warning; every visible string is Romanian. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

cards.plain: For any job with an estimate, the system shows line by line what was planned against what actually left the warehouse, in both quantity and money, including the material nobody planned for. That last column is the leak the business cannot currently see.

cards.title: Retur de materiale: surplus coming back from a site to stock, as the inverse of an issue, with the project credited.
cards.plain: Material that comes back from a site can be returned into stock, and the job it came from is credited for it. Today surplus has nowhere to go, so the stock figure and the job cost are both wrong in the same direction.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/returns.spec.ts` exits 0. returns.spec covers: a return against an issue raises computed stock by exactly the returned quantity; the project material cost falls by exactly the returned quantity times unit value; a return larger than the quantity issued for that product on that issue is refused with a Romanian message; the sum of returns against one issue line can never exceed what that line issued, proven by a second partial return that is refused; a return appears in the project Consum tab as a negative row and is visibly a return, not a negative issue; a return writes a status history row. Same RLS shape as everywhere else. A RETURN ALWAYS POINTS AT THE ISSUE IT CAME FROM, and a line always points at the issue line. A free-floating return with no source is an inbound delivery, which the system already has, and conflating the two would let stock be created out of nothing through a screen with no supplier and no document behind it. OVER-RETURN IS IMPOSSIBLE, ENFORCED IN THE DATABASE AND NOT ONLY IN THE FORM: the sum of returned quantity per outbound_line_id may never exceed that line quantity. Implement as a trigger or a checked function in the same migration, matching how the existing stock functions in 0003 and 0004 are written. A UI-only check is not a check. STOCK IS COMPUTED, NOT STORED, and the existing computation is extended rather than replaced: whatever function or view already derives available stock from batches minus issues gains minus-returns as a third term, in one place. Reading the current implementation first is part of this card, and if the computation turns out to be duplicated across screens, unifying it is in scope because the alternative is a return that raises stock on one screen and not on another. A RETURN IS NOT A DELETION AND NOT AN EDIT OF THE ISSUE. The issue stays exactly as it was. History is append-only across this whole system and this card does not make the first exception. THE RETURNED VALUE USES THE SAME BASIS AS THE COST REPORT, current unit_value_mdl, so a return credits a project by the same measure the issue debited it and the two cannot drift apart within one screen. cards.title: Documents per project and per client on Supabase Storage: contracts, acts, invoices and site photos, in the bucket that is already provisioned.
cards.plain: Contracts, acts, invoices and site photos attach to the customer or to the job they belong to, so the paperwork lives with the work instead of in somebody inbox. The storage for it is already set up and paid for.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/documents.spec.ts` exits 0. documents.spec covers: a file uploaded on a project appears in that project Documente tab and nowhere else; a file uploaded on a client appears in that client Documente tab; the file is readable ONLY through a signed link and a direct unsigned request is refused; an unauthenticated request for the object is refused; a file over the size limit is refused with a Romanian message naming the limit; a disallowed file type is refused with a Romanian message; deleting a document removes the row and the object and writes who did it; every visible string is Romanian. PLUS `ls supabase/migrations/*_documents.sql` exits 0 and its MIGRATION JOURNAL is recorded as evidence per CLAUDE.md 8.5, plus an APPLY LOG entry per P2-11.
cards.defaults: THE BUCKET IS THE ONE THAT ALREADY EXISTS. supabase/migrations/0002_rc_docs_bucket.sql provisions rc-docs and it is private, and the inbound order document upload already reads and writes it through signed links. This card reuses that bucket, that privacy model and that signed-link path, and does not create a second bucket. If the existing bucket or its policies turn out not to support a second document type, that is a finding and the halt rule applies. SCHEMA: public.documents (id; client_id uuid null references clients on delete restrict; project_id uuid null references projects on delete restrict; storage_path text not null unique; original_name text not null; mime_type text not null; size_bytes bigint not null; kind public.document_kind not null; notes text null; uploaded_by uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null; created_at). A CHECK CONSTRAINT enforces that exactly one of client_id and project_id is set: a document belongs to a client or to a project, never to both and never to neither. KIND IS AN ENUM WITH FIVE VALUES: create type public.document_kind as enum ('contract', 'act', 'factura', 'foto', 'altele'). The Romanian labels are Contract, Act, Factura, Fotografie, Altele. cards.title: Schema and module: outbound_lines freezes the unit value at the moment of issue, so a project cost total stops moving when somebody edits a product price.
cards.plain: A job's material cost is worked out from today's product prices, so changing a price silently rewrites what past jobs appear to have cost. This records the price onto the release at the moment it happens, the way an invoice does, and the warning currently printed on the screen comes off.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/project-cost-snapshot.spec.ts` exits 0. The spec covers, and the second case is the whole card: an issue is created against a project and the project cost total is read; the product's `unit_value_mdl` is then changed in the catalogue; the project cost total is UNCHANGED, to the leu, on both the total and the by-product breakdown; a NEW issue of the SAME product raised after the price change is costed at the NEW value, so one project legitimately holds two different unit values for one product and the total is their sum; a row issued before this migration still carries a value and is not null and not zero; and the Romanian footnote naming the current-catalogue caveat is GONE from the Cost tab, because it has stopped being true. PLUS `ls supabase/migrations/*_outbound_unit_value_at_issue.sql` exits 0, and `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 with that file in the set applied to the bare postgres.

THE COLUMN IS `unit_value_at_issue_mdl` ON `public.outbound_lines`, numeric(14,2) not null check (>= 0). The name is the one the AUTHOR wrote on P3-11 and it carries the currency suffix every other money column in this schema carries (unit_value_mdl, sale_price_mdl, budget_mdl, unit_price_mdl).

NOT NULL WITH A BACKFILL, NEVER NULLABLE WITH A FALLBACK. Add the column nullable, backfill every existing row from products.unit_value_mdl, then set not null in the same migration and the same transaction. A nullable column read as `coalesce(unit_value_at_issue_mdl, p.unit_value_mdl)` is a default-and-override, not a snapshot: it is indistinguishable from correct on the day it is built and diverges silently afterwards. R-058 named exactly that shape on the deviz price and rejected it, and the same reasoning binds here.

THE BACKFILL IS HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT CANNOT KNOW, IN A COMMENT IN THE FILE. Rows issued before this migration get today's catalogue value because no other value has ever existed. That is not a repair of history and the comment says so: this card freezes the value from now on, and the rows it backfills keep whatever drift they already had.

THE WRITE PATH IS THE ISSUE PATH AND NOTHING ELSE EVER UPDATES THE COLUMN. Whatever creates an outbound line today (see supabase/migrations/0004_outbound_functions.sql and 0018_outbound_issue_project_write.sql before writing anything new) reads the catalogue once, at insert time, and writes it. cards.plain: Make sure that a supplier written with dots, or with different accent marks, is recognised as the supplier already in the system instead of being added a second time.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 with an assertions file proving that, after normalisation, SRL and S.R.L. resolve to ONE supplier, and that a comma-below diacritic and a cedilla diacritic of the same name resolve to ONE supplier. PLUS: the WRITE path is covered, not only the lookup: a case proving that saving a product with a punctuation variant of an existing supplier name creates NO second row in public.suppliers. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults: TWO FINDINGS, ONE PROBLEM, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE CARD. FOLD-01 found that public.fold_text normalises case, diacritics and whitespace runs and does NOT touch punctuation, so Bricolaj SRL and Bricolaj S.R.L. are two suppliers and the write path creates the second. Andre hit the same class from the other side: comma-below versus cedilla diacritics. fold_text already translates BOTH forms, so his case may already fold; the card verifies that rather than assuming it, and the punctuation half is definitely open. THE WRITE PATH IS THE SUBJECT. lib/data/suppliers.ts resolveSupplier is now the single place both product-creation paths go through, which is what makes this card one change rather than two. A fix that only hardens the lookup leaves the create branch free to insert a near-duplicate. A CHANGE TO fold_text IS A CHANGE TO EXISTING DATA, and this is the trap: fold_text is IMMUTABLE and may be indexed, and widening it changes what already-stored rows fold to. If any index or generated column depends on it, the card either adds a NEW function and leaves fold_text alone, or rebuilds what depends on it in the same migration, and it says which in the PR. Decide by reading pg_depend, not by reading the migrations. NO MERGING OF EXISTING DUPLICATES IN THIS CARD. If production already holds two records for one supplier, merging them moves foreign keys and is its own card with its own evidence.

NO VERCEL API AND NO VERCEL_TOKEN, ON THE OWNER'S INSTRUCTION. VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA is exposed to the application at build time by the platform itself, so the deployed build can state its own commit with no credential at all. This SURVIVES P2-13's credential revocation, which is the point: a check that dies when the credentials rotate is a check that dies on the day it matters.

THE ROUTE IS PUBLIC AND CARRIES NOTHING ELSE. A commit sha and a migration version number. No environment names, no counts, no health of any dependency. Anything more is a card of its own, because a health route is the one endpoint everybody adds one more field to.

RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED IS REPLACED, NOT KEPT AS A FALLBACK. An operator statement that survives beside a machine check is the one that gets used at three in the morning. If the health route cannot be reached, the applier REFUSES; it does not fall back to asking.

THE LEDGER VERSION IS READ FROM THE DATABASE THE APP IS CONNECTED TO, never from the repository. The repository says what SHOULD be applied; only the database says what IS.
